name: multi_timeframe_breakout_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: A breakout that is confirmed on both the 1-min AND 5-min timeframes has significantly higher reliability than a breakout on either timeframe alone. The 5-min chart filters out noise that causes false breakouts on the 1-min chart, while the 1-min chart provides precise entry timing within the broader 5-min signal. Specifically, when a stock breaks above its 30-bar Donchian Channel on the 5-min chart AND simultaneously breaks above its 60-bar Donchian Channel on the 1-min chart, the breakout has multi-resolution confirmation. The edge exists because most traders trade on a single timeframe. Multi-timeframe analysis is well-known conceptually but rarely implemented systematically with real-time dual-feed computation. The inefficiency persists because multi-timeframe strategies are harder to backtest and deploy operationally.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 50 crore INR AND close > 100 INR

conditions: 5min_close > DC_upper_5m (5-min breakout confirmed on current or last completed 5-min bar)
long.confirmation: both timeframes showing new highs simultaneously (within the same 5-min bar)

short.confirmation: both timeframes showing new lows simultaneously

entry.entry_price: market order when dual-timeframe breakout confirmed

exit.target: 0.6% from entry (multi-timeframe breakouts tend to produce larger moves)
exit.signal_exit: exit if 5-min bar closes back inside its Donchian Channel (higher timeframe reversal)

filters.time_filter: no entries before 10:00 (5-min lookback of 30 = 150 min, so need ~2.5 hours; starts mid-morning from prior day close calc) or after 14:00
other_filters: 5-min Donchian must use at least 20 completed 5-min bars for reliability

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — dual-timeframe systematic breakout is operationally complex; few implement it

weaknesses: Dual-timeframe confirmation is very strict — many valid breakouts on one timeframe will not be confirmed on the other
The 5-min lookback of 30 bars = 150 minutes; intraday session is only 375 minutes, so data is limited early in the day
Operational complexity: need to maintain 1-min and 5-min bar feeds simultaneously with aligned timestamps
prior_art: Multi-timeframe analysis: Elder's Triple Screen System ('Trading for a Living') is the classic. Alexander Elder uses weekly + daily + intraday. Brian Shannon uses daily + hourly + 5-min. The specific dual-Donchian across 1-min and 5-min is a quantitative adaptation. Corey Rosenbloom ('The Complete Trading Course') discusses multi-timeframe Donchian channels.
notes: Edge math: 0.54 * 60bps - 0.46 * 35bps = 32.4 - 16.1 = 16.3 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ 5.3 bps per trade. Positive. One of the stronger breakout strategies due to dual-timeframe confirmation raising the win rate. Low trade frequency (0-2/day) is the trade-off for higher quality. Operational complexity is justified by the positive expected edge.
